tldr: For fixed labeled geometric clusters, assignment optimization conditional on the specified uncentered Horvitz--Thompson estimator has proved effective finite-program consequences: a variational risk evaluator, a closed saturation interval with certified endpoint brackets and endpoint inclusion, explicit interior attaining laws, rational both-arm samplers under the saturation promise, computable all-law positive-gap certificates, and a critical linear-versus-sublinear dichotomy. A structural equality criterion, a sampler derived from the structural critical family, critical-face branch selection, and a matched boundary scale remain open. The remaining critical question is whether optimal subset priors retain positive early-coordinate mass or escape to the head singleton. Independent midpoint-centered HT has strictly smaller worst-case actual MSE than the optimized raw rule throughout the infinite geometric regime. This is a conditional assignment benchmark for a user retaining raw HT, not all-estimator optimality or Wald inference.
